title: Neural-ODE for pharmacokinetics modeling and its advantage to alternative machine learning models in predicting new dosing regimens

content.abstract_summary: First application of neural-ODE to pharmacokinetic modeling, using trastuzumab emtansine PK data from two dosing regimens. Neural-ODE substantially outperforms alternative ML models (LSTM, transformer, etc.) when predicting an unseen dosing regimen, while performing comparably to alternatives within the training regimen. Establishes neural-ODE as the most accurate PK model for extrapolating to untested treatment regimens at the time of publication (Genentech / U Michigan, 2021).
key_findings: First study to apply neural-ODE to PK modeling — establishes feasibility and provides a benchmark for all subsequent neural ODE pharmacometrics papers

Neural-ODE showed substantially better performance than LSTM and other alternatives specifically for predicting an unseen dosing regimen (generalization beyond training conditions) — the clinically critical capability
Models performed similarly across methods when training and test sets come from the same dosing regimen — the key differentiation is extrapolation, not interpolation
Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) used as case study — two clinical dosing regimens, antibody-drug conjugate oncology PK
limitations: Case study uses a single drug (T-DM1) and two dosing regimens — generalizability to other drugs and more complex PK/PD structures is not demonstrated
No mechanistic hybrid — the neural ODE replaces the ODE system entirely rather than augmenting a known compartmental structure; identifiability not assessed
No population-level (NLME) modeling — individual-level only; IIV not addressed

extracted_claims.text: "To date, neural-ODE is the most accurate PK model in predicting untested treatment regimens."
"This study represents the first time neural-ODE has been applied to PK modeling and the results suggest it is a widely applicable algorithm with the potential to impact future studies."

gaps_addressed: Provides the foundational benchmark for M1.1 — establishes that neural-ODE outperforms alternative ML models for dosing regimen extrapolation, motivating hybrid mechanistic-ML over pure-ML approaches

Defines the key evaluation criterion for neural ODE PK models: prediction of unseen dosing regimens (not just held-out patients from the same protocol) — this should be the WG's standard benchmark for M1.4

provenance.notes: Found via PubMed search 'neural ODE pharmacokinetics pharmacodynamics' (PMID 34308294). Open access (PMC8283337). iScience 2021, 24(7):102804. Authors: Lu J (Genentech), Deng K & Zhang X (Ann Arbor Algorithms), Liu G (Genentech), Guan Y (U Michigan). Upgrade to full_text recommended — this is the foundational paper for M1.1 and the starting point for any WG review of neural ODE PK literature.
